questions.q: By default, when does an action in a Power Automate flow run relative to the action before it?
options: Only when the previous action is successful
Only when the previous action has failed
Always, regardless of the previous action's outcome
Only when manually triggered a second time
questions.explain: By default, an action's Run After setting is configured to run only when the previous action 'is successful,' which is why a single failure normally halts the entire flow.

questions.q: Which Run After checkbox would you enable to make an action serve as an error-handling step?
options: is successful
is skipped
has failed
has timed out and is successful, together only
questions.explain: Checking 'has failed' makes an action run specifically when the previous action didn't succeed, turning it into an error path.

questions.q: In the Scope-based try/catch pattern, what determines whether a Catch scope runs?
options: The Catch scope's Run After is set to fire when the Try scope has failed
The Catch scope runs on a fixed schedule independent of Try
The Catch scope always runs first, before Try
Catch scopes cannot be configured with Run After settings
questions.explain: The Catch scope's Run After setting is configured to trigger when the Try scope has failed, giving one clean failure path for everything grouped inside Try.

questions.q: What does the Terminate action do?
options: It pauses the flow until a human resumes it
It ends the flow immediately and sets an explicit status and message visible in run history
It restarts the flow from its trigger
It silently deletes the flow's run history
questions.explain: Terminate stops the flow outright and records a status (Succeeded, Failed, or Cancelled) with an optional message, preventing a failure from being mistaken for a completed run.

questions.q: According to the lesson, why does error handling matter more for flows that call AI model endpoints?
options: AI model calls never fail, so error handling is actually less necessary
Rate limits, timeouts, and malformed JSON responses are normal operating conditions for model APIs, not rare bugs
Power Automate automatically retries every AI Builder action without configuration
AI Builder actions cannot be placed inside a Scope
questions.explain: Unlike a mature connector like Outlook or SharePoint, a model endpoint can legitimately rate-limit, time out, or return malformed JSON as part of normal operation, making Run After and Scopes baseline hygiene rather than an advanced topic.
